title: Quick check: Route Handlers and Route Conflicts

questions.prompt: In the context of “Route Handlers and Route Conflicts” and “Coexisting pages and handlers”, What do parallel routes support in the App Router?
options: Rendering multiple named route slots within a shared layout.
Running SQL queries in parallel automatically.
Replacing authentication checks with separate page folders.
Adding query parameters without changing the route tree.
questions.answer_key: Rendering multiple named route slots within a shared layout.
questions.explanation: Parallel routes compose separate route slots; they are a routing/UI architecture feature rather than a database concurrency primitive.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Route Handlers and Route Conflicts”, What is a practical reason to use an intercepting route?
options: To show contextual content, such as a detail modal, while retaining the underlying page during client navigation.
To force every route to use a static export.
questions.answer_key: To show contextual content, such as a detail modal, while retaining the underlying page during client navigation.
questions.explanation: Intercepting routes can create modal-style navigation but require thoughtful fallbacks and direct-navigation behavior.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Route Handlers and Route Conflicts”, What should advanced route composition test?
options: Direct URL loading, browser back/forward behavior, refresh behavior, and the appropriate fallback UI.
Only whether the folder name exists.
Only a screenshot of the modal state.
questions.answer_key: Direct URL loading, browser back/forward behavior, refresh behavior, and the appropriate fallback UI.
questions.explanation: Routing composition has several navigation paths, all of which should behave predictably.
